outcome: neonatal outcomes (stillbirth, neonatal death, NICU admission)
postpartum complications (wound infection, fever, wound dehiscence, deep vein thrombosis)
cohort: 107 pregnant women with singleton pregnancies at >32 weeks gestation and BMI > 30 kg/m^2 who delivered at a single institute in India.
finding: Maternal obesity was associated with gestational diabetes mellitus, pre-eclampsia, need for labor induction, increased cesarean delivery, increased NICU admissions, and increased incidence of postpartum infections.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was the most common mode of delivery (52.34%), followed by cesarean section (40.19%) and instrumental delivery (7.48%).
birth_weight: Most common birth weight group was 2.5-3.99 kg (40.19 %), followed by 1.5-2.49 kg (34.58 %)
